title: Childhood asthma: focused assessment
opening: Hello nurse, I'm worried about my son. He's been coughing and breathing faster since last night.

facts.answer: His cough started yesterday evening. His breathing became worse this morning.
He has been coughing and I hear a whistling sound when he breathes out. He seems more breathless today.
He has a blue reliever inhaler. I gave him two puffs this morning using his spacer, but he still seems breathless. I don't remember the exact time.
He sometimes coughs when running and when the room is dusty. He also had a runny nose yesterday.
He has eaten less today, but he's still taking small sips of water. He passed urine this morning.
He doesn't want to play and stops to catch his breath when talking. He is awake. I haven't noticed blue lips.
A doctor told us he has asthma about a year ago. He visited the emergency department once last year but has never needed intensive care.
He sometimes coughs at night, perhaps twice a week. I don't think he uses a daily preventer inhaler.
I don't know of any medication allergies.

assessment.label: Vital signs
assessment.finding: Illustrative findings: HR 132/min, RR 38/min, SpO₂ 93% on room air, temperature 37.2°C. Verify against your institution's age-specific guidance.

assessment.label: Work of breathing
assessment.finding: Subcostal and intercostal recessions are visible. He speaks in short phrases and appears distressed.

assessment.label: Auscultation
assessment.finding: Bilateral expiratory wheeze with reduced air entry at both bases.

assessment.label: Consciousness and colour
assessment.finding: Alert, anxious, and responsive. No central cyanosis observed.

assessment.label: Hydration and perfusion
assessment.finding: Mucous membranes slightly dry; capillary refill approximately 2 seconds. Reassess with the full clinical picture.

safety_message: This child has concerning respiratory findings in this fictional scenario. In a real setting, promptly seek senior clinical help and follow local paediatric deterioration and acute asthma protocols. Do not delay escalation to complete a checklist.
